instructions:
GOAL: Add the seven straightforward projectile / AoE / aura weapons from the GDD to the game's weapon system so each is addable via addWeapon() and fires deterministically. This is a Cosmo Canyon Ready Spec for Realm Survivors (Vite + TS + PixiJS v8, deterministic sim + Pixi renderer).

IMPORTANT PATH CORRECTION: The weapon FIRE LOGIC lives at src/sim/systems/weapons.ts, and the weapon DATA lives at src/sim/data/weapons.ts. (The spec's `files` list says "src/sim/weapons.ts" as a shorthand for the fire logic — the real file is src/sim/systems/weapons.ts. Edit src/sim/systems/weapons.ts, NOT a new src/sim/weapons.ts.) Renderer is src/render/stage.ts.

HARD RULES (must obey):
- NEVER edit anything under game/test/** or game/accept/** — these are tamper-guarded. Do not add, rename, or modify test files. Your changes must keep the EXISTING gate green (tsc typecheck + the existing tests in test/, especially test/determinism.ts, test/sim-purity.ts, and test/sim.weapons.ts).
- src/sim/** must stay deterministic: NO Math.random, Date.now, performance.now, or requestAnimationFrame anywhere under src/sim/. The sim's only randomness source is the seeded RNG (state.rng, class Rng in src/sim/rng.ts). The sim-purity test (test/sim-purity.ts) greps for these four APIs under src/sim/ and hard-fails if any appear in real (non-comment) code. src/render/** MAY use performance.now / rAF (it is presentation only).
- Placeholder art is fine — do NOT create real PNGs. New fx.* texture keys auto-declare as labeled grey-box placeholders the first time getTexture(key) is called (see src/assets/registry.ts getTexture/declare), so you do NOT need to edit any manifest for placeholders to work.
- Keep maxLevel at the literal value 3 for every new WeaponDef. The WeaponDef.maxLevel field is typed as the literal `3` in src/sim/data/weapons.ts and the existing test/sim.weapons.ts rarity loop iterates the pool assuming that shape. Do NOT widen maxLevel to 5 (the GDD mentions level 5 but the type is pinned to 3 — leave it; per-level damage already scales via damageForLevel()). Changing the literal type is OUT OF SCOPE and will risk the gate.

EXISTING SHAPES YOU ARE EXTENDING (read these files first to confirm):
- src/sim/data/weapons.ts exports: `type WeaponBehavior = 'straight-up' | 'spread-nearest' | 'aoe-nearest' | 'spread-explosive' | 'straight-up-explosive'`; `interface WeaponDef { id; name; cooldown; behavior: WeaponBehavior; baseDamage; maxLevel: 3; rarity }`; `function damageForLevel(def, level)`; and `const WEAPON_POOL: WeaponDef[]` (existing ids: axe, knives, fireball, bomb-kunai, viking-spread, fire-axe, ragnarok, infinite-kunai, god-spread).
- src/sim/systems/weapons.ts exports `addWeapon(s, weaponId)` and `weaponSystem(s)`. weaponSystem computes the single NEAREST enemy once per tick (nearestX/nearestY/hasTarget), then per weapon slot ticks `slot.timer -= FIXED_DT` and when it fires branches on `def.behavior`. It has helpers spawnProj(s, dirX, dirY, damage), spawnExplosiveProj(s, dirX, dirY, damage, explosionTimer, explosionRadius, explosionDamage), and triggerExplosion(s, x, y, radius, damage). Projectiles are a flat pool (s.projectiles); Projectile shape is in src/sim/state.ts: { id, x, y, vx, vy, damage, maxRange, travelled, hit, explosionTimer?, explosionRadius?, explosionDamage? }. AoE-style behaviors increment s.weaponAoeFires (the snapshot exposes weaponAoeFires; tests key off it).

ADD THESE SEVEN WEAPONS. For each: add a WeaponDef entry to WEAPON_POOL in src/sim/data/weapons.ts with the exact id, name, cooldown, behavior, baseDamage, maxLevel:3, rarity; and ensure src/sim/systems/weapons.ts fires it correctly (reuse an existing behavior branch where the mapping fits, or add a NEW branch in the `if (def.behavior === ...)` chain and a NEW string in the WeaponBehavior union only where noted). Give each a distinct fx.* texture in src/render/stage.ts (see rendering section).

1. SHURIKEN — id 'shuriken', name 'Shuriken', rarity 'common'. GDD: shoots straight forward, PIERCING. Mapping: reuse a single straight projectile toward nearest (like the 'straight-up' branch's spawnProj toward nearest direction — note the existing 'straight-up' branch actually fires toward nearest via nx/ny), BUT it must PIERCE (pass through enemies, damaging each, instead of despawning on first hit). Piercing needs a new projectile field. Add an OPTIONAL boolean field `pierce?: boolean` to the Projectile interface in src/sim/state.ts (and to makeProjectile()'s reset if you reset all fields — set pierce:false there / or leave undefined and treat falsy as non-pierce). Add a spawnPiercingProj helper (or extend spawnProj with an optional pierce param) that sets proj.pierce = true. In the projectile move/hit loop of weaponSystem, when a projectile with pierce===true hits an enemy: apply damage, add to totalDamageDealt, push to deadEnemies if hp<=0, but DO NOT set proj.hit = true and DO NOT push it to toRelease for that collision — let it keep travelling until it reaches maxRange. To avoid re-hitting the SAME enemy every tick while overlapping, either (a) give the piercing projectile enough speed that it clears an enemy radius in one tick (acceptable), or (b) track a small per-projectile hit set — prefer (a) for simplicity and determinism (no allocations). Behavior string: add a new WeaponBehavior 'straight-pierce' and a branch that calls the piercing spawn toward nearest (nx, ny). cooldown ~0.9, baseDamage ~22.

2. WAND OF FIREBALL — id 'wand-of-fireball', name 'Wand of Fireball', rarity 'common'. GDD: AoE. Mapping: reuse the EXISTING 'aoe-nearest' behavior (instant AoE blast centered on nearest enemy, increments s.weaponAoeFires). No new branch needed — just set behavior:'aoe-nearest'. cooldown ~2.0, baseDamage ~50.

3. THROWING KNIVES (fan of 3) — id 'throwing-knives', name 'Throwing Knives', rarity 'common'. GDD: three straight forward in a fan. Mapping: reuse the EXISTING 'spread-nearest' behavior (fires center + left + right offset by SPREAD_DELTA). No new branch needed — set behavior:'spread-nearest'. NOTE: the existing pool already has an id 'knives' named 'Throwing Knives'; use a DIFFERENT id 'throwing-knives' and a slightly different name to avoid collision (e.g. name it 'Throwing Knives (Fan)' or 'Kunai Fan' so it is visibly distinct). cooldown ~0.8, baseDamage ~18.

4. JAVELIN — id 'javelin', name 'Javelin', rarity 'rare'. GDD: throws ONE projectile at a target — explicit contrast to Throwing Knives (three in a fan). Mapping: a SINGLE straight projectile toward nearest. This is distinct from Throwing Knives (3) by firing exactly one. It could reuse 'straight-up' (which fires one toward nearest) — but to keep it clearly its own weapon and allow a longer range / higher single-hit damage, add a new WeaponBehavior 'javelin' whose branch calls spawnProj(s, nx, ny, dmg) exactly once (single projectile toward nearest). Keep it non-piercing (contrast with Shuriken). cooldown ~1.3, baseDamage ~45 (higher single hit than knives).

5. CROSSBOW — id 'crossbow', name 'Crossbow', rarity 'rare'. GDD: fires at the CLOSEST enemy; high damage, long cooldown. Mapping: a single straight projectile toward nearest (targeting is already nearest-based). Reuse 'straight-up' OR the new 'javelin' branch — but set a LONG cooldown and HIGH baseDamage to express the GDD contrast. cooldown ~2.5 (long), baseDamage ~90 (high). If reusing 'straight-up' is ambiguous with axe, use the 'javelin' single-projectile branch. Use fx.crossbow_bolt for its visual.

6. GREATSWORD — id 'greatsword', name 'Greatsword', rarity 'rare'. GDD: high-damage sweep in front of the character. Mapping: an instant melee AoE (a short-range sweep), NOT a travelling projectile. Add a new WeaponBehavior 'sweep-front' and a branch that does an INSTANT AoE damage pass over enemies within a sweep radius in FRONT of the player toward the nearest enemy. Implement as: compute a sweep center point at the player position offset toward nearest by ~50px (center = player + (nx,ny)*50), then damage all enemies within a radius (~90px) of that center — reuse the same collect-then-kill pattern as the 'aoe-nearest' branch (iterate s.enemies.forEachActive, subtract dmg, collect dead, killEnemy after loop; also hit destructibles the same way). Increment s.weaponAoeFires so the AoE-fire counter/tests see it. cooldown ~1.6, baseDamage ~70 (high). Deterministic — uses nearest direction, no rng.

7. HOLY SYMBOL — id 'holy-symbol', name 'Holy Symbol', rarity 'rare'. GDD: constant AoE aura around the character. Mapping: an instant AoE centered on the PLAYER (not on nearest enemy) that fires on a short cooldown so it reads as a constant aura. Add a new WeaponBehavior 'aura-self' and a branch that damages all enemies within an aura radius (~110px) of the PLAYER position (s.player.x/y), collect-then-kill pattern, also hit destructibles, increment s.weaponAoeFires. Fires regardless of hasTarget is fine, BUT note the current weaponSystem early-returns the whole slot loop step when `!hasTarget` (it sets slot.timer=0 and continues). For an aura you WANT it to still pulse with no enemies in range — however to keep determinism and avoid restructuring, it is acceptable to let the aura only pulse when hasTarget is true (there's nothing to damage otherwise, so behavior is observably identical). Keep the existing hasTarget guard; the aura simply does its player-centered AoE in its branch. cooldown ~0.6 (frequent, aura-like), baseDamage ~20.

WEAPONBEHAVIOR UNION CHANGES (src/sim/data/weapons.ts): extend the WeaponBehavior union to include the new strings you introduce: 'straight-pierce' (shuriken), 'javelin' (javelin/crossbow single shot), 'sweep-front' (greatsword), 'aura-self' (holy-symbol). Wand-of-fireball reuses 'aoe-nearest' and throwing-knives reuses 'spread-nearest' (no new strings for those two). Add the matching branches in src/sim/systems/weapons.ts's behavior if/else chain. After adding branches, the chain must handle every behavior value so tsc + runtime stay correct.

PROJECTILE STATE CHANGE (src/sim/state.ts): add `pierce?: boolean;` to the Projectile interface for Shuriken. If makeProjectile() explicitly lists fields, either add pierce:false or leave it out (undefined = non-pierce). Ensure spawnProj / spawnExplosiveProj set/reset pierce appropriately (non-piercing spawns should leave pierce falsy, otherwise a reused pool slot could stay piercing). This is the ONLY new projectile field this spec needs.

RENDERING (src/render/stage.ts): projectiles are currently drawn generically (the sim's projectile pool is rendered by the stage). To give each new weapon a distinct look, wire an fx.* texture per weapon using getTexture(key) from src/assets/registry.ts. Assign textures as follows: Shuriken -> fx.shuriken; Wand of Fireball -> fx.wand_fireball; Throwing Knives (fan) -> fx.throwing_knife; Javelin -> fx.javelin; Crossbow -> fx.crossbow_bolt; Greatsword -> fx.greatsword; Holy Symbol -> fx.holy_aura. These are seeded Ready placeholder keys and will render as labeled grey boxes until real art exists — that is expected. If the current stage draws all projectiles as identical Graphics circles with no per-weapon identity, at minimum call getTexture() on each of these keys somewhere in the render path so the keys are declared and visible in the wishlist, and draw the instant-AoE weapons (Greatsword sweep, Holy Symbol aura) as a brief circle/arc at the correct center (player for aura, player+offset for sweep) using its fx key or a colored circle. Full per-projectile sprite skinning is nice-to-have; the load-bearing requirement is that each new fx.* key is referenced in stage.ts so it appears and can be swapped for real art later. Keep the renderer deterministic-friendly (performance.now is allowed here but not required).

DETERMINISM / ACCEPTANCE (you must NOT edit test/**, so satisfy the EXISTING gate and describe manual/visual checks):
- The existing test/sim.weapons.ts rarity loop asserts every pool weapon's rarity matches a rule: ids bomb-kunai/viking-spread/fire-axe => 'rare'; ragnarok/infinite-kunai/god-spread => 'legendary'; ALL OTHER ids => 'common'. Therefore any NEW weapon you mark 'rare' (javelin, crossbow, greatsword, holy-symbol) WILL BREAK that test's else-branch which expects every other id to be common. CRITICAL: to keep the existing gate green WITHOUT editing tests, set the rarity of ALL new weapons in this spec to 'common'. (The GDD lists these as Tier-1 primary weapons; 'common' is the correct tier anyway. Re-tune rarity later via a separate spec that also updates the test — out of scope here.) So: shuriken, wand-of-fireball, throwing-knives, javelin, crossbow, greatsword, holy-symbol => rarity 'common'. Adjust the per-weapon rarity notes above accordingly: use 'common' for all seven.
- Determinism gate (test/determinism.ts) runs 1200 ticks twice with the default loadout and asserts byte-identical snapshots. Your new behaviors only execute if a new weapon is equipped, so the default run is unchanged — BUT still ensure NO new nondeterminism: no rng in the new branches, integer/float math only, no iteration over unordered structures. Pool iteration via forEachActive is already deterministic (slot order); mirror the existing branches exactly.
- Self-verification you SHOULD run locally (do not commit test files): write a THROWAWAY scratch script under game/.claude/scratch/ or a scratch_*.ts (gitignored) that: newGame(seed), sets player.attackTimer=99999 to disable the base AoE, sets player.weapons=[{weaponId:'shuriken',level:1,timer:0}], spawns a line of low-hp enemies, runs ticks, and asserts a projectile is spawned AND at least one enemy dies (and for shuriken, that one projectile passes through and damages 2+ enemies in a line = piercing). Repeat for each new weapon: for aoe/aura/sweep weapons assert snapshot().weaponAoeFires increases and enemies die; for javelin/crossbow assert exactly one projectile spawns per shot; for throwing-knives assert 3 spawn per shot. These mirror the style of the existing test/sim.weapons.ts checks. Delete the scratch file before finishing. The permanent proof is: tsc passes, existing tests pass.

VISUAL NOTE: After wiring, run the game (Vite dev + Claude Preview) and confirm each new weapon, when equipped, visibly fires: piercing shuriken passes through a row of enemies; wand-of-fireball and holy-symbol produce AoE flashes; greatsword flashes a sweep in front; javelin/crossbow send single bolts; throwing-knives sends a 3-fan. The fx.* placeholders will look like labeled grey boxes/circles — that is acceptable for a Ready spec. Confirm no console errors and the game does not crash when these weapons are equipped.
